claims.text: Pressure-assisted infiltration at approximately 1300–1400 K will create a refined tungsten skeleton.
Pressure-assisted infiltration at approximately 1300–1400 K will produce a more uniform distribution of copper.
Pressure-assisted infiltration can minimize porosity in W–Cu composites.
Pressure-assisted infiltration can strengthen W–Cu interfacial bonding while limiting interfacial reactions.
Reduced porosity and improved W–Cu interfacial bonding enable efficient heat conduction through a continuous copper phase.
A refined tungsten skeleton preserves mechanical strength.
A refined tungsten skeleton mitigates radiation damage and provides irradiation-damage tolerance.
The intervention will increase thermal conductivity by approximately 10–20% relative to a conventionally infiltrated W–Cu composite.
The intervention will maintain mechanical durability at elevated temperatures.
The intervention will maintain irradiation resistance under fusion-reactor-relevant exposure.
Conventionally infiltrated or lower-temperature-sintered W–Cu composites have higher porosity than the proposed composite.
Conventionally infiltrated or lower-temperature-sintered W–Cu composites have less uniform W–Cu interfaces than the proposed composite.
Higher porosity and less uniform W–Cu interfaces reduce thermal conductivity in the baseline composite.
Excessive processing pressure or temperature can cause W–Cu interfacial reactions.
W–Cu interfacial reactions caused by excessive processing conditions negatively affect mechanical behavior.
Insufficient infiltration pressure may leave residual porosity.
The proposed performance should hold during elevated-temperature exposure and high helium or neutron flux.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires mechanical durability and irradiation resistance to be maintained, for which equality with the reference would ordinarily suffice. The falsification rule instead states that equal or lower durability and radiation resistance would falsify the hypothesis, making an outcome claimed as successful elsewhere count as failure.
